newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures close a little higher.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures close a little higher.

text.p: Key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures rose on Friday in a generally quiet market as investors waited for the result the general election to be held in Japan on Sunday.

Dealers said the rise was a rather technical one. A city bank trader said it was on short-covering and squaring of short positions created after a senior politician's comment about the possibility of a supplementary budget after the election.

The contract slipped on Wednesday when Taku Yamazaki, a senior MP from the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), which is forecast to win most seats in the election, said a supplementary budget worth about five trillion yen should be considered after the polls.
Dealers said, however, that the slippage also revealed that the contract was firmly supported around 99.10. "There were a lot of buy-backs below 99.09," the city bank trader said.
But on the topside, good performance of Tokyo share prices on Friday curbed the June contract at around 99.15.
In the interbank call market, the key overnight rate was steady, mostly at 0.47 percent, the level which dealers said was likely to be the weighted average for the day.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) conducted its usual neutral operation, injecting 200 billion yen into the market to offset a fund shortage of about 220 billion yen.
The rate broke with its recent tendency to fall on a Friday.
"The market knows that the BOJ would tighten its operation if the rate falls too far -- below 0.45 percent," a dealer at a city bank said.
Rates in the open market were also stable, with the benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) issued at an unchanged 0.52 percent. About 145 billion yen worth have been reported issued.
One- and two-month CD rates were also pegged at their recent levels, at 0.49 percent and 0.50 percent, respectively. Issue volume was about 20 billion yen each.
Interest in the two shorter-period issues was waning as the rates looked too low for investors, compared with the latest level of the overnight rate, a trader at a city bank said.
